title: Variables & data types
examples: When should I use a float instead of an integer?
What is the difference between a string and a character?
Can I change a data type in programming?

explain.say: Today we look at variables and data types in coding.

draw.text: Data Types: int, float, string, Boolean

explain.say: An integer or int stores whole numbers without any decimal points.
A float stores numbers that have decimal points, like measurements.
A string holds text characters, like names or sentences you write.
A Boolean only stores two values: true or false for logic checks.
Casting means changing a data type from one to another type.

faq.q: What is the main difference between an integer and a float?
faq.a: An integer is for whole numbers only, while a float allows for numbers with decimal places.
asks: When do I use int versus float?
What is the difference between whole numbers and decimals?

faq.q: Can I use letters and numbers in a string?
faq.a: Yes, a string can hold any combination of letters, numbers, and symbols characters.
asks: Is a string just for words?

faq.q: What does Boolean mean in programming?
faq.a: Boolean deals only with logical states, which are either true or false.
asks: What are the two values for Boolean?
Does Boolean only deal with yes or no?

faq.q: Why do I need to cast data types?
faq.a: You must cast data when you need to use a number in a calculation that expects a different format.

faq.q: If I have the number 5, can I treat it as a string?
faq.a: Yes, you can convert the number 5 into the string "5" if you need to display it as text.
asks: How do I make a number look like text?
Can I change a number to a string?

facts: Integers (int) represent whole numbers, like -3, 0, or 50.
Floats (float) are used for real numbers, such as 1.5 or -0.75.
Strings (string) are sequences of characters enclosed in quotes.
Booleans (Boolean) represent truth values: true or false.

quiz.say: Which data type should store the number of students in a class?
quiz.why: The number of students is a whole number, so an integer is the correct choice.

wrong.0: Boolean only stores true or false, not a count of items.
wrong.2: A float implies a decimal measurement, which is not needed for counting people.
wrong.3: A string treats the number as text, which prevents mathematical calculations.

quiz.say: If you read the text "Grade A" into a variable, what is its data type?
quiz.why: Because the variable contains letters, it must be stored as a string data type.

wrong.0: Floats are for numbers with decimal points, not for alphabetical text.
wrong.1: Boolean can only store true or false, not descriptive text like grades.
wrong.3: Integers cannot store letters; they are restricted to whole numbers only.

quiz.say: If you have the string "15" and need to add it to the integer 10, what must you do first?
quiz.why: To perform addition, both values must be the same type, so you cast the string to an integer.

wrong.0: This would result in text concatenation, not mathematical addition.
wrong.1: Ignoring the string means you lose the data you were trying to use in the calculation.
wrong.2: Changing to a float might introduce unnecessary decimal points to the result.
